where: Worked example 1, step 5 and the answer line
problem: The trace mixes a query() call with getType(). ContentResolver.query() never calls getType(); getType() is reached only when someone calls getContentResolver().getType(uri) (for example to decide whether a URI is a directory or a single item). The caller also never sees the UriMatcher code — that number stays inside the provider. A student will read the answer as if the Cursor comes back carrying a MIME type and a match code.
fix: step 5: inside the provider, match(uri) returned 2, so if getType() is asked for this URI it answers vnd.android.cursor.item/com.example.marks.students. answer: The caller receives only a Cursor with 1 row (_id 2, Ravi, 72 marks). The match code 2 is internal to the provider; the item MIME type is returned only by a separate getContentResolver().getType(...) call.

where: Section 3, exam traps and quiz Q4
problem: "Authority in code and manifest differ; every URI returns NO_MATCH" is only half true. If the caller's URI carries the authority from the code (UriMatcher) and the manifest registered a different one, the resolver finds no provider at all and throws IllegalArgumentException (unknown URL); NO_MATCH is returned only when the URI matches the manifest authority but the UriMatcher was built with a different string.
fix: Write: if the URI authority does not match android:authorities, ContentResolver fails to find the provider and throws IllegalArgumentException. If the manifest authority and the string used in addURI() differ, the provider is found but every URI reaching it returns NO_MATCH.

problem: The custom permissions READ and WRITE are declared on the provider, but the chapter never says the other app must request them. Without that step the client gets a SecurityException even when the provider is exported.
fix: Add: the calling app declares <uses-permission android:name="com.example.marks.READ"/> (and WRITE) in its own manifest, and the <permission> elements should set android:protectionLevel, for example signature, so only apps signed with your key get access.

problem: ContactsContract.Contacts.CONTENT_URI cannot be read with the few lines shown unless the app holds READ_CONTACTS. On Android 6.0 and later that is a runtime permission request, so the code fails with SecurityException as written.
fix: Note that reading a built-in provider also needs the matching permission, for example android.permission.READ_CONTACTS declared in the manifest and granted at runtime with requestPermissions() before the query.

problem: The label 'query(uri, null, null)' shows a three-argument call, but ContentResolver.query() and ContentProvider.query() take uri, projection, selection, selectionArgs and sortOrder. The label can teach a wrong signature.
fix: Label it query(uri, projection, selection, selectionArgs, sortOrder) or simply query(uri).
